name: Turning Whisper into a Real-Time Transcription System (Whisper-Streaming)
problem: Whisper is a non-streaming 30s-window model, so naive streaming to it either blocks for 30s or transcribes unstable prefixes.
mechanism: Local agreement policy: run the Whisper decoder on every incoming buffer and emit only the longest prefix on which the current hypothesis and the previous hypothesis agree, with a self-adaptive latency that delays the rolling buffer until agreement stabilises. Buffers are re-encoded on every step, so the encoder runs repeatedly per utterance rather than once.
speedup_reported: Reports 3.3 s latency on an unsegmented long-form speech test set, and demonstrates production use as a live transcription component at a multilingual conference. The number is a latency figure on the authors' own test set with no GPU specified, so treat it as a demo-scale result.
notes:
Published as an IJCNLP-AACL 2023 system demonstration (arXiv comment). The mechanism matters for anyone serving Whisper: local agreement re-runs the encoder-decoder over the buffer every step, so the encoder cost scales with (steps x buffer length) rather than with audio length. That is the price of retrofitting streaming onto a fixed-window model, and it is why production streaming ASR uses Conformer/Zipformer transducers instead. Recorded here as the in-repo representative of the 'Whisper VAD / segmentation / chunking' family.
